A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InstanceAssemble and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Their methods and experiments can be reliably matched across renumbering, relocation, and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations on LayoutSAM-Eval, DenseLayout, and COCO-Layout, together with component ablations, control-ratio experiments, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds bounding-box-encoding and attention-mask comparisons in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The layout encoder, instance-wise attention and assembling, cascaded interactions, LoRA adaptation, Section 3.4 training objective, and early-stage control schedule are retained. Newly specified initialization, rank, and adapted blocks document the implementation without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Training remains on LayoutSAM, with evaluation on LayoutSAM-Eval, DenseLayout, and COCO-Layout. Textual conditioning, image/depth/edge conditioning, and style-LoRA demonstrations retain the same task coverage. The added ablations vary model components rather than introduce new datasets or task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds an attention-mask comparator alongside an SD3-Medium base-model control. Conversely, the unadapted Flux.1-Dev and Flux.1-Schnell baselines from v1 Table 6 disappear from the consolidated DenseLayout comparison. The other benchmark comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds experimental configurations that remove bbox encoding separately from DenseSample and substitute attention-mask injection. Existing training budgets, resolutions, metrics, and denoising schedules remain unchanged. The newly disclosed LoRA settings and explanations of existing ablation controls do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: New Appendix B separates the contribution of bbox encoding from DenseSample and tests Assemble-Attn against attention-mask region injection. These are focused extensions to the retained component ablation and control-ratio sensitivity analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report experimental point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The DenseLayout instance-count distribution statistics are also unchanged.

E6.justification: New entries include 51.22 mIoU without bbox encoding or DenseSample in v2 Table 6, and attention-mask spatial/VQA scores of 94.11/91.53 in Table 7. Matched existing benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged. The unadapted Flux DenseLayout rows are removed, and the guard-and-cannon qualitative example is replaced by a candle example.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces the noise-prediction LDM preliminary objective and discrete timestep description with continuous-time interpolation and a flow-matching velocity objective. This corrects the background mathematical formulation to agree with the already-existing Section 3.4 training loss; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: instance-assembling attention, lightweight adaptation, multimodal layout control, DenseLayout, and LGS. Claims about dense-layout performance and style compatibility retain their scope; the abstract's added resource-access statement concerns reproducibility.

C2.justification: v2 adds the specific limitation that image fidelity can degrade under extremely dense or complex layouts. Appendix B.2 also introduces a mechanism explanation involving semantic leakage from global attention masks in overlapping regions and the benefits of cropped instance-wise attention.

D1.justification: v2 specifies pretrained initialization, LoRA rank 4, adaptation of all SD3 blocks versus eight Flux blocks, and the parallel-interaction/full-fine-tuning meanings of existing ablation controls. The abstract also adds a repository link and states that code and pretrained models are publicly available.

R1.justification: v2 expands the explanation of the already-cited GrounDiT approach, adds Lipman et al.'s flow-matching reference, and removes the Prodigy reference while retaining that optimizer. These are limited changes to attribution and positioning.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites expand the preliminaries, implementation details, dense-layout discussion, ablation explanation, and limitations. v2 adds an ablation appendix and acknowledgments, moves dataset documentation, and updates author/affiliation and conference information. The introduction and most scientific exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the DenseLayout radar panels with a consolidated main-text table drawn from earlier appendix tables, adds two ablation tables, and expands the component-ablation caption. It also replaces one qualitative example and relocates several displays. Most figures and the overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves clarity and reproducibility through consistent flow-matching preliminaries, explicit implementation and ablation details, resource-access information, and focused additional controls. The new density-related limitation also better qualifies applicability. These limited gains outweigh the loss of unadapted Flux comparison rows, although the new attention-mask table leaves its dataset and spatial metric insufficiently specified. The core method and established numerical results remain unchanged.
